fullDescription: A help center / support site UI on a deep bottle-green ground that indexes every answer by WHERE IT LIVES on the product screen. Instead of a list of article titles, the hero is a grid of six cream crops of the actual product UI, each with a single marked hotspot showing where that answer lives, so a stuck user navigates by pointing rather than by guessing what a control is called. Below it, one worked example: the full product panel with numbered marks sitting on the real controls and short action-only instructions joined by hairline connectors. One grotesk at light and medium weights, flat fills, hairline borders, no gradients. Reusable for any help center, knowledge base, product documentation site, onboarding guide, or in-app support surface.
prompt:
## Resumo
A HELP CENTER / SUPPORT SITE (desktop 1440, fully responsive) for a data-workspace product, on a deep bottle-green #0a2e0e ground with cream #faf5e8 panels and a single peach #fcab79 mark colour. The organising idea: the unit of help is not an article but a LOCATED ANSWER, so the site is indexed by WHERE each answer lives on the product screen rather than by title or category. ONE grotesk (Plus Jakarta Sans) does everything at weights 400 and 500 ONLY, hierarchy from SIZE; IBM Plex Mono appears only on step numbers and the status line. Every band on the page shares ONE content measure (max-width ~1180px, centred). Top: a slim masthead (wordmark left; Docs / API / Status / Log in right in cream), a 34px/400 'Gridwork help' H1, then a full-width cream SEARCH FIELD with near-black ink — the primary action, plain and high-contrast, in the ordinary place. HERO (the argument): a section 'Where each answer lives' — SIX cream tiles, 3 across at desktop / 2 at tablet / 1 at mobile, each a legible ~360x200 CROP of a DIFFERENT region of the SAME product screen (view-tab bar left, view-tab bar right past '+ Add', a column header, the right end of the header row, the row-number gutter, an empty cell under a status pill), drawn in the panel's own treatment (cream field, mid-green left rail only where the crop includes the left edge, 18%-opacity hairlines, a 5% header wash, real type icons, real status pills), each carrying exactly ONE peach mark with a 1px near-black ring placed precisely where that answer lives, with the answer title and a small right-aligned step count beneath. Content bleeds off the tile edges so they read as windows onto one screen, not six separate cards. Then ONE WORKED EXAMPLE: the full cream data-grid panel (green left rail, view-tab bar with one tab active, icon column headers, numbered rows, hairline grid lines, colour-coded single-select status pills) with THREE ringed peach marks sitting ON the actual controls, each joined by a short 1px peach connector to a small cream label carrying an ACTION-ONLY instruction ('Open this menu, choose Single select'), so the connector carries the noun and the words carry only the verb. Then a plain 'Billing and account' list of four hairline-ruled text rows for answers with no control to point at; a status line banded between two mid-green hairlines; an in-flow 'Still stuck?' cream panel with a solid peach CTA pill; and a multi-column footer. Flat fills, hairline borders, 12px button radii, 16px panel radii. NO gradients anywhere, no dot-grid or line-grid texture, no sticky bars, no uppercase letter-spaced micro-labels.

## Estilo Visual
Design a help center / support site for a data-workspace product on a deep bottle-green #0a2e0e ground. Use cream #faf5e8 for every panel and crop, and reserve peach #fcab79 ENTIRELY for hotspot marks, their connectors, and the primary CTA, so that anything peach is a thing pointing at something. Use sky-blue #c7e5f2 and mid-green #214224 only as status-pill fills inside the product panel, and near-black #181d26 as ink on cream. Give every peach mark and the CTA a 1px near-black ring so they out-ink the cream they sit on. Set ALL type in ONE grotesk (Plus Jakarta Sans) at weights 400 and 500 only, never bold, with hierarchy from size: 34px H1, 22px section heads, 15px body, 13px UI labels; add IBM Plex Mono only for step numbers and one status line. Keep every band on the page to ONE shared content measure. Flat fills, hairline borders, 12px button radii, 16px panel radii. Absolutely NO gradients, no dot-grid or line-grid background texture, no uppercase letter-spaced micro-labels, no sticky bars, and no drop shadows beyond a faint ambient.

## Layout e Estrutura

### Masthead, page title and search
Set a slim masthead on the green ground: wordmark left in cream, and Docs / API / Status / Log in as plain cream text links right. Below it a 34px / weight 400 cream H1 naming the site ('Gridwork help'). Directly under that a FULL-WIDTH search field: a cream #faf5e8 rounded rectangle about 56px tall with a small near-black search glyph and near-black placeholder text ('Search Gridwork help'). Do NOT put a micro-label above the field and do NOT centre this block — it is a plain, high-contrast primary action in the ordinary place. At mobile, stack the wordmark above the nav row rather than cramming both onto one line.

### The location index (this is the hero and the whole idea)
Under a 22px cream heading 'Where each answer lives', lay out SIX tiles in a 3-across grid (2 at tablet, 1 at mobile) filling the full measure. Each tile is a cream #faf5e8 panel about 360x200 containing a LEGIBLE CROP of a different region of the SAME product screen, drawn in that screen's own treatment: 18%-opacity mid-green hairlines, a 5%-opacity header wash, real column-type icons, real status pills, and the mid-green left rail ONLY on crops that include the screen's left edge. Let content bleed off the crop edges so each tile reads as a window onto one larger screen rather than a separate card. Place exactly ONE peach mark — a filled ~26px disc with a 1px near-black ring — precisely where that answer lives, and make the placement semantically correct: the row-number gutter for 'select several rows at once', an actually-empty cell for 'filter out records with an empty cell'. Beneath each tile put the answer title in cream at 15px/400 on the left and a small muted step count right-aligned. Keep all six tiles the same height; nothing here is drawn to scale.

### The worked example (annotated product panel)
Below the index, under a 22px cream heading naming one task and a short muted line of context, render the FULL product panel as a large cream card: a mid-green left accent rail, a view-tab bar with one tab active under a 2px underline plus a '+ Add' tab, a header row with icon column headers, three numbered rows carrying record names and small initial chips, hairline grid lines, and colour-coded status pills in the final column. Place THREE ringed peach marks with mono step numbers sitting exactly ON the controls the task uses, and join each by a short 1px peach connector to a small cream label. The label text must be ACTION-ONLY with no positional description — 'Open this menu, choose Single select', 'Open this header, then Edit options', 'Rename this option' — so that covering the connectors makes the instructions unresolvable. Never park the instructions in a numbered legend away from the panel, and never write a line describing what the annotation system does. At mobile keep every column visible and every mark on its control, and move the three instructions directly beneath the panel numbered to match.

### Answers with no screen, status band, contact and footer
Add a plainly-titled section ('Billing and account') holding four cream text rows separated by mid-green hairlines, deliberately plainer than the index above — no crops, no marks. Then a single status line in IBM Plex Mono at 12px, banded between two full-measure mid-green hairlines ('All systems operational. Sync last checked 4 minutes ago.') with named states only and no bars or charts. Then an IN-FLOW cream panel spanning the full measure, two columns: a 22px near-black heading, a short intro and a solid peach CTA pill with near-black text and a 1px ink ring on the left; a four-item bulleted list of what to include in a ticket on the right. Never make this bar sticky. Close with a mid-green hairline and a footer: wordmark left, three link columns in cream.

## Componentes Especiais de UI

### Screen-crop location tile — The page's signature component and its entire organising idea: a cream tile holding a legible crop of one region of the real product screen, with a single ringed peach mark placed exactly where that answer lives. Six of them index the help content by LOCATION instead of by title, so a stuck user matches what is on their own screen to a picture rather than guessing the noun for a control.
Build a ~360x200 cream #faf5e8 tile containing an inline SVG crop of one region of a product UI, rendered in that UI's own treatment: 18%-opacity mid-green hairline rules, a 5%-opacity header wash on any header row, real column-type glyphs, and real status pills in their true fills. Let text and rules run off the tile edges so it reads as a window onto a larger screen; include the left accent rail only if the crop contains the screen's left edge. Place exactly ONE filled ~26px peach #fcab79 disc with a 1px #181d26 ring at the precise coordinate the answer concerns, in clear space so it never covers a label. Beneath the tile set the answer title at 15px/400 and a small right-aligned muted step count. Build six of these covering six DIFFERENT regions of the SAME screen and lay them out three across.

### Pinned instruction with connector — A hotspot mark sitting on a real control, joined by a hairline connector to a short action-only instruction. The connector carries the noun and the words carry only the verb, so the instruction cannot be understood without the pointing — which is what stops the pattern collapsing into an ordinary numbered list.
Place a filled ~28px peach #fcab79 disc with a 1px #181d26 ring and a mono step number directly ON a control inside a rendered product panel, positioned to graze rather than cover the control's label. From the disc's edge draw a 1px peach connector that terminates exactly on the edge of a small cream #faf5e8 label with near-black 13px/400 text. Write the label as an ACTION ONLY, using a deictic with no referent in the text — 'Open this menu, choose Single select', not 'Open the + Add menu at the end of the view tabs'. Verify the connector starts on the mark edge and ends on the label edge rather than floating near either. At narrow widths keep the disc on its control and move the labels beneath the panel as a numbered list matching the disc numbers.

### Product data-grid panel — The object being documented, drawn at real fidelity so the annotations have something true to point at. It is subject matter rather than the design: it is deliberately demoted below the location index so the page's identity comes from what was done to the grid, not from the grid itself.
Render a cream #faf5e8 rounded panel as a database/spreadsheet view: a mid-green left accent rail, a view-tab bar carrying three view names plus a '+ Add' tab with the active tab marked by a 2px underline, a header row with a leading checkbox and icon-plus-label column headers, three numbered rows with record names and small square initial chips, hairline grid rules at 18% opacity, and colour-coded single-select status pills in the final column (a pale sky fill, a solid mid-green fill with cream text, and a cream outline). Keep every row the same height. At mobile rebalance the column widths so all columns stay visible rather than introducing horizontal scroll.

### Hairline-banded status line — A one-line system-status band that reports NAMED states only. It deliberately avoids the uptime-bar grid every status page reaches for, so nothing on the page is drawn to scale and there is no second visual system competing with the marks.
Set a single line of IBM Plex Mono at 12px in cream ('All systems operational. Sync last checked 4 minutes ago.') with about 16px of padding above and below, bounded top and bottom by full-measure 1px mid-green #214224 rules. Report named states in words only. Do not add uptime bars, a 90-day grid, a chart, a coloured status dot row, or any element whose length or area encodes a quantity.

style.description: A dark TECHNICAL-MANUAL register, not a marketing page and not a default support template. The whole page sits on a deep saturated bottle-green #0a2e0e, which is doing real work: it is a committed chromatic ground rather than the hedged near-black-plus-one-accent that generated work reaches for, and it makes the cream panels read as physical inserts laid onto a field. Cream #faf5e8 carries every panel and every crop; peach #fcab79 is reserved ENTIRELY for marks, connectors and the primary CTA, so anything peach is by definition a thing pointing at something; sky-blue #c7e5f2 and mid-green #214224 appear only inside the product panel as status-pill fills; near-black #181d26 is the ink on cream. Contrast is arithmetic, not taste: cream 13.68:1, peach 7.97:1 and sky 11.29:1 on the ground, ink 15.53:1 on cream. Because peach on cream is only 1.72:1, every peach mark and the CTA carry a 1px near-black ring so the load-bearing marks out-ink their own container. ONE grotesk (Plus Jakarta Sans) does all type at 400/500 ONLY — never bold or black — with hierarchy from size alone, and IBM Plex Mono is rationed to step numbers and the status line. Shapes are flat: hairline borders, small radii, no shadow beyond a faint ambient. There are NO gradients in the file at all, no background texture, and no uppercase letter-spaced labels.
